mathematical_result.statement: At every global Gaussian heat mode y_* of any finite positive law, the Gaussian-tilted standardized residual U=(Z-y_*)/epsilon satisfies E exp(vU)<=exp(v^2/2) for all real v; conversely this MGF condition characterizes global heat modes.
mathematical_result.qform_compiler: If C_* is the scale-invariant optimal QFORM density constant and S_R is the fixed-radius centered small-ball ratio evaluated at the best global unit-Gaussian heat mode, then S_R<=C_*<=[2R/(sqrt(2pi)(1-R^-2))]S_R for R>1. At R=sqrt(3), the factor is 3sqrt(3)/sqrt(2pi)=2.072964896828013.

partner_applied.application: Used the exact heat-height identity plus scalar homogeneity to obtain C_*=sup_A s_3(A) max_y E gamma_1(Q_A-y), then derived the mode-centered small-ball comparison.

regularity_context.scope: Every fixed rank>=3 target instance has an individually bounded C_0 density; constants are matrix dependent and do not settle universal height.

unresolved_implication: Prove a uniform bound on the mode-centered fixed-radius small-ball functional S_sqrt3 using original-coordinate product geometry, preferably in the low-volume/high-leverage or minority/two-sheet endpoint before any fiber supremum or reciprocal-small-minor payment.
